name: MathlibAnnex.Sphere.finrank_eq
title: Isometric unit spheres force equal finite dimensions

content.display_title: Isometric unit spheres force equal finite dimensions
content.one_sentence_role: Compares Hausdorff dimensions in both directions using the surjective Lipschitz radial maps.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $X,Y$ be finite-dimensional real normed spaces and let $\Delta:S_X\to S_Y$ be a bijective isometry for the chord metrics inherited from their ambient norms. Here $S_X=\{u\in X:\|u\|=1\}$ and $S_Y=\{v\in Y:\|v\|=1\}$ are the unit spheres. Then

$$\dim_{\mathbb R}X=\dim_{\mathbb R}Y.$$
content.assumptions: Both $X$ and $Y$ are finite-dimensional in this exact theorem. Each carries a real normed-space structure and $\Delta$ is a sphere isometry equivalence. If only one space is known to be finite-dimensional, the separate transfer theorem first supplies the other hypothesis. No positive-dimension assumption is needed.
content.conclusion: The natural-number dimensions of the two real vector spaces agree. The intermediate invariant is the Hausdorff dimension of the entire ambient metric space, which is an extended nonnegative real number; its identification with linear dimension is a separate finite-dimensional theorem.
content.proof_summary:
Write $\dim_H(X)$ for the Hausdorff dimension of the whole metric space $X$. The map $R_\Delta:X\to Y$ is $3$-Lipschitz, and the inverse identities show it is surjective. The Lipschitz range theorem therefore gives

$$\dim_H(Y)=\dim_H(R_\Delta(X))\le\dim_H(X).$$

For the inverse sphere isometry, $R_{\Delta^{-1}}:Y\to X$ is likewise surjective and $3$-Lipschitz, giving

$$\dim_H(X)=\dim_H(R_{\Delta^{-1}}(Y))\le\dim_H(Y).$$

Thus the Hausdorff dimensions are equal. For each finite-dimensional real normed space the Hausdorff dimension of the whole space equals its real-linear dimension, viewed in $[0,\infty]$. Applying that theorem to both spaces and using injectivity of the natural-number cast gives the asserted equality of linear dimensions.

proof_steps.text: Use the forward radial map with the Lipschitz range bound, then replace its range by all of $Y$ using surjectivity. This proves the inequality in the direction from $Y$ to $X$.

Repeat with the inverse sphere isometry to obtain the opposite inequality. Hence the Hausdorff dimensions agree. For finite-dimensional real normed spaces these equal the real-linear dimensions, including in dimension zero.

content.lean_realization_notes: The proof compares the forward and inverse radial maps. It neither uses an unproved invariance of topological dimension nor identifies either radial map with a linear map.
